rejected.title: Earthquakes
card: An earthquake is a shaking of the ground. It happens when rock along a fault, a crack in the Earth's crust, slips suddenly.
Stress builds up as rock on each side of a fault is pushed or pulled. When the rock finally gives way, the stored energy is released as waves that shake the ground.
Impacts can include collapsed buildings, landslides on steep slopes and fires from broken gas pipes and power lines.
Harm is usually worst where buildings are weak and many people live close together. The same shaking can cause far less damage where buildings are strong and fewer people live.
rejected.remember: A sudden slip along a fault causes an earthquake. Weak buildings and dense populations make the harm worse.

a.q: Stress has built up in the crust near a fault. Which event then shakes the ground?
opts: The rock along the fault slips suddenly
The rock along the fault slowly wears away
Heavy rain loosens soil on a nearby slope
Waves from the ocean hit the coast
a.why: When the stressed rock gives way and slips, the stored energy is released as waves that shake the ground. Slow wearing away of rock is erosion, which does not suddenly release energy.
a.clue: Think about what happens along a crack in the crust.

b.q: One earthquake shakes four towns equally hard. Which town is likely to suffer the most harm?
opts: Poorly built homes, with many people packed close
Well-built homes, with many people packed close
Poorly built homes, with a few farms spread apart
Well-built homes, with a few farms spread apart
b.why: Harm is usually worst where buildings are weak and many people live close together, and only the first town has both. A town with poorly built homes but few people spread apart has fewer people near each building that might fall, so less harm is likely.
b.clue: The card names two things that make harm worse.

b.q: Two towns in different countries have the same strong earthquake. Town A has weak buildings and crowded streets. Town B has strong buildings and fewer people. Why is Town A likely to suffer more harm?
opts: Weak buildings and dense population increase the damage
Its earthquake releases more energy than Town B's
Fires only start in towns that have crowded streets
Landslides only happen in towns with weak buildings
b.why: The earthquake is the same, so the difference comes from how well buildings stand up and how many people are close by. The energy released is not the reason, because the shaking was the same in both towns.
b.clue: The earthquake was the same size in both towns.

a.best: The rock along the fault slips suddenly

b.best: Weak buildings and dense population increase the damage

problems.detail: Two distractors use 'only' ('Landslides only happen…', 'Fires only start…'), absolute claims that are easy to rule out. The right option also restates the stem's 'weak buildings and crowded streets', and the clue rules out the energy option. A student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.
